subject: Post-demo: cloud privacy, data paths & subprocessor list
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex@neptunehealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: cloud privacy, data paths & subprocessor list

Hi Alex — great running through the demo earlier. Thanks for the time. Quick recap and the security items we agreed to follow up on: 

- You asked for our SOC 2 scope and the most recent Attestation report (Type II). I attached a short snapshot that summarizes scope and control owner contacts.
- Please share Neptune’s current list of subprocessors (cloud infra, analytics, logging, email, monitoring) and any HIPAA/GDPR-specific controls that apply to those vendors.
- We need a high-level data flow diagram (PII/PHI boundaries, egress points) so we can confirm alignment on retention and encryption-in-transit/rest.
- Action: we’ll send a short subprocessor questionnaire to your security team to capture TLS, key management, and access controls.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_snapshot.pdf (application/pdf)

If you can send the subprocessor CSV and a link to your privacy contact, we’ll get the questionnaire over the next business day. Proposed next step: security touchpoint call with Soojin (our security lead) and your security team — are mornings (PST) on Thursday/Friday better for you?

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com | (415) 555-0122

--
From: Alex Green <alex@neptunehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Neptune Security Team <security@neptunehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cloud privacy, data paths & subprocessor list

Logan — thanks for the clear summary and the SOC snapshot. Appreciate it. Attaching our current subprocessor roster (exported). High level notes:

- Core infra: AWS (us-west-2) — EC2, S3, EKS.
- Observability: Datadog (logs/metrics), Sentry (errors).
- Payments: Stripe (tokenized, no card raw storage).
- Email/notifications: SendGrid.
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions (hosted).
- Analytics: Amplitude (product metrics).

We do process limited PHI in a subset of integrations (labs ingestion) — that will be in the data flows. Neptune is HIPAA-covered; we maintain BAAs with vendors handling PHI. Our primary ask: we need confirmation about Redwood’s handling of PHI (if any) and any subprocessors Redwood relies on that will touch Neptune data.

Attachment: neptune_subprocessors.csv (text/csv)

We can do a security call Friday 11:00–11:45am PST if that works. I’ve looped our security alias.

Best,
Alex Green
Head of Product | Neptune Health
alex@neptunehealth.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex@neptunehealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cloud privacy, data paths & subprocessor list

Alex — thanks for the CSV and the proposed time. We can confirm Friday 11:00am PST for a 30–45m security sync. A few items our team wants to capture ahead of the call so we can make it productive: 

1) PHI scope: can you flag which Neptune data feeds contain PHI (labs, clinical notes, device telemetry) and whether that data is tokenized/encrypted client-side?
2) Retention: typical retention windows for the PHI-bearing datasets and if any are subject to legal hold policies.
3) Processing: which of the listed subprocessors have BAAs in place (you noted Stripe and the labs partners) — please indicate yes/no in the CSV next to each vendor if possible.
4) Cross-border: is any of the PHI processed or stored outside the US for your tenants?
5) Access model: do Neptune personnel use SSO with SCIM provisioning and role mapping to limit access?

We’ve attached a draft subprocessor questionnaire we’ll use to collect vendor controls (TLS versions, KMS usage, SOC 2/ISO attestations, encryption at rest). If Neptune can pre-populate the CSV with BAA and region flags before Friday, we’ll be able to focus the call on the items that need remediation or formal BAAs.

Attachment: subprocessor_questionnaire-draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Logan — I’ll capture any Redwood subprocessors that may touch Neptune data (we use GCP for some isolated inference clusters, and a small set of managed services for logging/monitoring). I don’t expect Redwood to be a processor of PHI by default — we treat customer data as customer-controlled — but we need the call to confirm deployment mode and contractual terms (BAA requirement).

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Security Lead | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com

Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: cloud privacy, data paths & subprocessor list

Team — quick internal alignment following Alex’s notes and Soojin’s questions:

- Action owner: Marissa, please lead the BAA/contracting thread once security confirms the PHI processing scope. I’ll include legal for signature cadence.
- Soojin, please confirm whether Redwood’s GCP inference clusters and our managed logging provider require any additional controls or a separate subprocessor entry beyond what we publish. If so, list the control gaps we need to remediate for Neptune.
- Aditya, schedule the Friday 11:00 PST security sync with Neptune and send a calendar invite to their security alias + Alex. Ensure the invite includes the data_flow_diagram.png (placeholder) and the questionnaire link.

Next steps for Friday call (agenda):
1) Confirm PHI feeds and whether data is client-side tokenized.
2) Review subprocessor roster and flag vendors requiring BAAs.
3) Agree on data residency and retention windows.
4) Capture any contract-level asks (BAA, audit rights, breach notification SLA).

I’ve attached a draft data flow image to the invite and re-attached the SOC snapshot for Neptune’s reference.

Attachments: data_flow_diagram.png (image/png), Redwood_SOC2_snapshot.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks — I’ll own follow-ups to ensure we have all evidence for procurement.

Logan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com
